## Summary

The reduction methods `sum`/`prod`/`mean`/`var`/`std` with `axis` + `skipna=True` already worked correctly for 2D masked arrays — the wrapping layer (`_wrap_reduction_result`) already computes the right NA mask via `self._mask.all(axis)` / `self._mask.any(axis)`. The problems were confined to three specific paths, all fixed in source (no test files touched):

### `pandas/core/array_algos/masked_reductions.py`

1. **`_minmax` (min/max) was fully broken for 2D axis reductions.** It used `values[~mask]`, which flattens a 2D array — so `axis=1` raised an `AxisError` and `axis=0` produced a wrong scalar. Added a 2D-axis branch that fills masked entries with a neutral value (global max for `min`, global min for `max`) so they never win the per-axis reduction, then reduces along the requested axis. All-NA rows/columns are masked by the caller.

2. **`_reductions` and `_minmax` returned a scalar `pd.NA` for `skipna=False` with an axis on 2D.** Because `mask.any()` is a global check, any NA anywhere collapsed the whole result to a scalar. Added a 2D-axis branch that computes over all values and lets the caller mask the affected rows/columns.

3. **`mean`/`var`/`std` early-abort guards** (`if not values.size or mask.all(): return NA`) now only short-circuit to a scalar in the 1D / `axis=None` case, so a fully-NA column yields a per-position `pd.NA` in an array rather than aborting early.

### `pandas/core/arrays/masked.py`

4. **`_wrap_min_count_reduction_result`** applied an all-`False` mask whenever `min_count == 0`, ignoring `skipna`. This caused `sum`/`prod` with `axis=0, skipna=False` to return `[5, 7, 9]` (unmasked) instead of masking columns containing NAs. Gated that shortcut on `skipna` being `True`; for `skipna=False` it now falls through to `_wrap_reduction_result`, which masks any column with a missing value.

All existing tests pass (masked, integer, floating, extension, reductions, frame reductions — ~12,000 tests), and `axis=None` results match the raveled 1D result across all seven reductions.
